newsitem.title: FRANCE: France renews calls for Zaire talks over rebellion.
newsitem.headline: France renews calls for Zaire talks over rebellion.

text.p: France on Saturday renewed calls for a ceasefire and talks to end a rebellion in Zaire after ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko returned home hoping to rally crumbling government resistance.
"New military actions will resolve nothing and will only lead to further violence and destruction," a foreign ministry spokesman said.

"We continue to hope that the entire international community will be able to convince all parties of the need of dialogue and of a peaceful solution," he said, expressing support for peace efforts by U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun.
"The search among Zaireans of an agreed electoral process that can give Zaire representative, stable and legitimate institutions must be the priority of all," he said.

Defence Minister Charles Millon said that Paris had taken necessary measures to protect its 1,500 citizens in Zaire. France has sent about 100 troops to nearby Congo and Gabon and has urged its nationals to leave if possible.
Millon ruled out any wider military action, perhaps to bolster France's long-time ally Mobutu, 66, insisting the reinforcements were merely "to ensure the security of our citizens".
He told Europe 1 radio that any evacuation would take 48 hours at the most.

France has been Mobutu's last international ally after almost 32 years in power. On Friday, Paris welcomed his call for a truce and national unity as positive steps that could help resolve the deepening crisis.
U.N. envoy Sahnoun was due in Zaire's northeastern city of Kisingani on Saturday to press rebel leader Laurent Kabila for a ceasefire following Mobutu's return.
The ministry spokesman said that "we continue to give all our support to the action of Mr Sahnoun...and his five point peace plan until it is effectively and fully put in place."
Mobutu left hospital in Monaco on Wednesday after fresh cancer treatment and flew home on Friday.
